Only `l`, `i` and `n` were edited, in `units.json`, by script. `t`, `ln`, `v` and `p` are unchanged (checked after the edit). The file's one-space indent is preserved.

## Considered and refused

- 1665 `Ofslōh` (1sg) is taken as “I slew”. The glossary and the note agree, and the context (“Then at that strife …”) fits.
- 1661 `ðȳ wǣpne gebrǣd` “I drew that weapon”. It is a disputed case relation (instrumental or dative). The note already says it is a guess, and nothing here is better grounded.
- 1661 note on the manuscript leaf at `hangian` (fol. 166b, A). I cannot check the apparatus abbreviation against anything but the packet, and the note matches the packet.
- 1668 `i` “out of my foes' hands”. The “my” and “hands” are English implied by `fēondum`, not a change of sense.
- 1698 `i` “the wise king”. `se wīsa` is Hrothgar, as the note says, and `l` keeps “the wise one”.
- 1700 `i` “born the better man”. The comparative with no stated comparison is already explained in the note.
- 1735 `dweleð` “hinder” in `l` against “troubles” in `i`. Both are within the lexical range and the force is the same.
- 1684 `be sǣm twēonum`: the note calls `twēonum` a dative plural noun, “between the two”. The lexica treat it as a fixed phrase; the note's gloss is adequate.
- 1728 “his selfa … his unsnyttrum”. The note already says the grammar is uncertain, and no better reading is available from the lexica.
- Remembered English: nothing in `i` is a known phrase from a translation. “Listen!”, “friend mine” and the rest are house renderings. “wise with winters”, “a wonder to say” and “joyless, he lived on” are rebuilt from the glosses.

## Not found

Case, tense, mood and negation were checked word by word in all 40 units. Apart from the points above, no further error was found.
